question: Can the already-cached Qwen3-1.7B checkpoint run a minimal HiddenBench full-information vote screen on the local GPU with lower CPU pressure than the prior Qwen3-8B setup?
scope: A resource and model/task capability screen only. It does not compare communication methods or models, and it does not establish protocol value.

model.name: Qwen3-1.7B
model.format: safetensors, loaded as float16 on CUDA by the project-local Transformers endpoint
model.runtime: Project-local Transformers endpoint; PyTorch 2.6.0+cu124; Transformers 5.2.0; one local CUDA device; two PyTorch CPU threads; one server worker; below-normal process priority

decoding.thinking: disabled by local Qwen chat template

design.control_reference: The Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M v0.8 screen passed 4/4 votes on this same full-information task and seed, using a different model, decoding configuration, and backend.
design.outcome: Official HiddenBench initial individual-vote accuracy and majority accuracy.
design.eligibility_gate: Eligible for a separately preregistered follow-up only if all four votes are correct and the resource limits are respected. Any incomplete, malformed, or truncated vote makes this screen incomplete and ineligible.
design.raw_data: Private prompt/fact/vote records and per-request usage logs stay under ignored .cache/pilot_hiddenbench_v0_9/. Publish only sanitized aggregates.

resource_safeguards.launch_gate: Three host CPU samples averaged below 25%; NVIDIA GPU utilization below 50%; GPU memory use below 2500 MiB; at least 6000 MiB system memory is free; port 8000 is unused; required local artifacts and runtime are present.
resource_safeguards.automatic_stop: Stop runner and local model service after host CPU is at least 65% for two consecutive 15-second samples, or GPU utilization is at least 90% for two consecutive 15-second samples.
resource_safeguards.no_progress_stop: Stop if the model service fails to become ready within 120 seconds or the runner exceeds 600 seconds.
resource_safeguards.telemetry: Sample host CPU, server CPU cores, server working set, GPU utilization, and GPU memory every 15 seconds. The server logs only request ID, token counts, generation/request durations, and finish reason; it never logs prompts or generated content.
resource_safeguards.cleanup: Terminate and wait for the runner and local model service from a PowerShell finally block.

predictions: If all four full-information votes are correct inside the resource envelope, this cached 1.7B setup becomes a lower-resource candidate for future study; no hidden-information ability follows from that pass.
If the model misses the 4/4 gate, stop this model/task line without a communication-format comparison.
If the resource gate rejects launch or an automatic stop fires, record a resource-infeasible result and do not retry with relaxed thresholds in this study.
limits: One task, one seed, and four votes are only a screening operating point.
The v0.8 Qwen3-8B reference changes checkpoint, precision/quantization, runtime, decoding, and backend; this is not a causal model-size or hardware comparison.
Full-information success does not demonstrate hidden-information solvability, communication benefit, protocol superiority, generalization, or a cost advantage.
Local endpoint usage logging measures request token counts and service time, not total system energy or a universal latency metric.
